Eight to twelve large pumpkins, each roughly 30-50 cm across, still attached to thick dried vines that run across the soil, resting and tilting in different directions among broad dry leaves, clods of earth and tangled stems — exactly the way pumpkins grow in a real garden. CONCEPT
An intensely realistic amateur recording inside an abandoned Five Nights at Freddy’s pizzeria. The protagonist films themselves at the beginning, then turns the camera forward and encounters an animatronic that physically and relentlessly approaches.

The main horror mechanic is distance compression: the protagonist sees the animatronic from far away, hides behind an obstacle, and loses visual contact. While the camera faces the wall, the animatronic continues moving through the real space and gets closer. When the protagonist cautiously peeks out, the corridor appears empty. Then the camera shifts slightly closer, revealing the animatronic suddenly standing directly in front of the lens.

CAMERA
The entire video is footage recorded by the protagonist’s phone. Never show the phone, its screen, its body, or the hand holding it.

The first 2 seconds are a frightened selfie. The protagonist then turns the camera forward. From that point until the end, remain strictly in handheld first-person POV. No external angles, repeated selfie, or cutaways.

The camera follows body movement: footstep impacts, sudden retreat, lateral inertia, rapid turns, cautious peeking around a pillar, and a panicked backward jerk. While hiding, the camera remains almost still and faces the wall or the side of an arcade cabinet.

AESTHETIC
An abandoned pizzeria lit by dirty-yellow ceiling lamps mixed with gray-green service-corridor light. Deep shadows, checkerboard flooring, old tables, arcade cabinets, dusty walls, a closed stage, and faded party decorations.

Raw 2000s consumer digital-camera texture: noticeable shadow noise, limited detail, clipped lights, limited dynamic range, brief autofocus hunting, compression artifacts, and strong natural motion blur during panicked movement. No glossy cinematic image, decorative VHS effects, or computer-generated glitches.

The animatronic is heavy and physically convincing. It does not teleport or appear from nowhere. Its torso lags slightly behind its steps, its head turns with mechanical inertia, its feet land heavily on the tile, and its joints creak. It can physically walk around a pillar or corner and become closer while outside the camera’s view.

SEQUENCE
0–2 seconds — Frightened selfie.

The protagonist from @image1 films themselves inside the dark pizzeria dining room. Their face is lit by a weak phone light, but the phone itself is never visible. They breathe heavily and whisper, “Quiet… there’s someone here.”

Deep behind their shoulder, a tall motionless figure is briefly visible between arcade machines. It nearly blends into the shadows. The protagonist notices movement, looks sharply toward it, and turns the camera forward.

2–5 seconds — First appearance at a distance.

The camera reveals the main dining area. A battered Chica stands approximately 12–15 meters away between the tables, partially hidden behind a row of arcade cabinets.

She does not attack immediately. First, she slowly turns her head, then begins walking directly toward the camera with fast, heavy mechanical steps. Every step has weight. The floor subtly vibrates, and her joints produce dry metallic creaks.

The protagonist watches for several seconds, unable to process what they are seeing. Chica takes one suddenly faster step, and the protagonist backs away.

5–8 seconds — Panicked hiding.

The camera abruptly turns aside. The protagonist runs several meters and dives behind a large concrete pillar or a tall row of arcade cabinets.

The camera presses close to the side of the cover. The frame contains mostly a dirty wall, the edge of the arcade machine, and trembling light. The protagonist breathes heavily, trying to stay silent.

Chica’s approaching footsteps can be heard outside the frame. They should not become instantly close: first distant, then noticeably nearer. Between the footsteps, the animatronic’s metal body scrapes against tables and arcade cabinets.

8–12 seconds — The animatronic passes the cover.

The camera remains hidden and does not show Chica. Her footsteps can be heard:

step… step… step…

They become louder. A metallic scrape follows, as if the animatronic is walking around the pillar or catching the edge of an arcade machine.

A moving shadow briefly crosses the wall beside the camera, then disappears. The protagonist continues waiting. Their breathing becomes quieter, but the camera trembles slightly from tension.

The footsteps suddenly stop.

12–16 seconds — Empty corridor and unexpected reveal.

The protagonist slowly peeks around the cover. First, only the edge of the pillar enters the frame. The corridor ahead appears empty. No one is visible in the distance.

The camera cautiously moves farther out. Empty tables and flickering lights are visible. It appears that Chica has left.

The protagonist slowly shifts the camera slightly closer to the corner. At that exact moment, Chica is already standing less than one meter from the lens. She physically walked around the cover from the opposite side while the protagonist was looking down the empty corridor.

She leans motionless toward the camera. Her head suddenly turns toward the lens. Her face and open beak fill most of the frame.

The reveal must be sudden but physically logical: Chica did not teleport. She silently moved around the obstacle while the protagonist was looking in the wrong direction.

16–20 seconds — Pursuit and cut-off.

Chica suddenly steps toward the camera and reaches out. The camera violently pulls back and turns away.

The protagonist starts running again. The image shakes strongly but realistically with each step. Tables and arcade machines rush past the frame edges. Heavy footsteps follow behind, much louder than before. Chica is no longer simply walking—she is accelerating and actively pursuing the protagonist.

The protagonist turns sharply around a corner. The camera strikes a wall or doorframe, producing a brief smear. Chica’s approaching heavy feet enter the frame. She has almost caught up.

Before her face fully enters the shot, the recording cuts off during the camera movement.

AUDIO
Raw built-in microphone audio only:

heavy breathing;
fast footsteps on tile;
distant footsteps gradually approaching;
mechanical joint creaks;
the animatronic’s body striking tables;
rattling arcade cabinets;
fluorescent hum and flicker;
a sharp servo sound just before Chica appears;
loud pounding footsteps during the final pursuit.
During the hiding section, the audio must communicate shrinking distance. The footsteps begin far away, pass behind the wall, and suddenly stop. After a short silence, Chica appears extremely close.

No background music or musical jump-scare effects.

NEGATIVE PROMPT
Visible phone, phone screen, phone reflection, external camera angles, repeated selfie, unexplained monster teleportation, Chica appearing without a physical route, constant unreadable camera shake, slow motion, cartoon animation, sliding feet, weightless movement, plastic-looking sets, computer glitches, excessive gore, titles, recording interface, and watermarks.

Pixar-quality 3D animated short film, 15 seconds, 16:9, titled "The Lost Ghost". A single continuous heartwarming sequence: a tiny lost ghost desperately searches an endless magical castle labyrinth for a way out, and finally finds freedom. High-end Pixar / DreamWorks feature-film rendering — cinematic global illumination, soft subsurface glow on the translucent ghost, tactile marble-and-stone textures, jewel-toned stained-glass light pooling and reflecting on the floor, gentle depth of field, volumetric light shafts, drifting dust motes, expressive squash-and-stretch, big appealing eyes, magical storybook-gothic atmosphere with playful comedic timing.

CHARACTER (keep perfectly consistent every shot):
THE GHOST — a small round friendly Pixar-style ghost, soft glowing translucent pale-blue/white body with subsurface glow and a wispy trailing tail, big expressive eyes, tiny stubby arms, faintly luminous, leaving a soft glowing light trail as it floats and darts. Endearing and highly readable — its emotion carries the whole film (hope, worry, panic, dizziness, exhaustion, joy).

SETTING (identical world every shot): an endless Pixar-rendered castle labyrinth — towering arched cathedral windows of glowing stained glass casting coloured light, sweeping Escher-style spiral stone staircases twisting in impossible directions, polished black-and-white checkerboard marble floors with soft reflections, dark stone archways and doorways leading nowhere, vaulted ceilings, mysterious repeating architecture. A magical maze with no obvious exit.

TIMELINE (8 beats — match storyboard timecodes EXACTLY):
00:00–01:52 — WIDE ESTABLISHING. The vast castle labyrinth revealed; a huge impossible spiral staircase sweeps through glowing stained-glass halls above a reflective checkerboard floor. The tiny glowing ghost floats alone at the bottom, small and lost in the enormous space. Slow lonely push-in, coloured light pooling, dust motes drifting.
01:52–03:45 — MEDIUM. The ghost drifts hopefully toward a large glowing arched doorway, big curious eyes, warm stained-glass light washing over it, soft glowing trail behind — searching for the way out. Gentle hopeful float.
03:45–05:37 — CLOSE-UP. The ghost peeks around a stone archway with hopeful eyes — only to find ANOTHER identical hall and spiral staircase beyond. Its face falls, eyes widening with dawning realisation. Emotional beat.
05:37–07:30 — LOW-ANGLE DYNAMIC. The ghost suddenly speeds off, zipping up a twisting Escher spiral staircase, wispy tail and glow streaks streaming behind it — the frantic search begins. Energetic upward motion, fast camera follow.
07:30–09:22 — HIGH-ANGLE. Looking down from above, the tiny ghost darts across the polished checkerboard marble floor between towering stained-glass windows, dwarfed by the endless maze, coloured light beaming down in shafts. Sweeping overhead move.
09:22–11:15 — DYNAMIC. The ghost rockets through a chain of looping arches and doorways that curve impossibly back on themselves, passing the SAME stained-glass window twice — comedic dizzy confusion, spiral eyes, spinning stars, wobbling in place. Playful Escher-loop gag.
11:15–13:07 — CLOSE-UP. The exhausted, defeated little ghost slumps and droops in mid-air above the checkerboard floor, glow dimming, tiny tears welling in big hopeful-sad eyes, wispy tail sagging. The lowest emotional point, quiet and tender.
13:07–15:00 — WIDE. A tall stained-glass window suddenly swings open — cool moonlight and night air pour in. The ghost's face lights up with pure joy, it beams a big happy smile and zooms toward the glowing open window, bright trail streaking behind it — freedom found at last. Uplifting final push toward the moonlit exit.

CAMERA: cinematic Pixar framing matching the 8-panel storyboard exactly — wide establishing push-in, hopeful medium, emotional close-up, energetic low-angle chase-up, sweeping high-angle overhead, dizzy dynamic loop, tender close-up, uplifting wide finale. Varied shot sizes, no repeated angle in a row.
MOTION: floaty ghost drift with expressive squash-and-stretch, bursts of fast darting flight up the staircase (05:37) and through the loops (09:22), dizzy spinning at 09:22, a slow tired droop at 11:15, and a joyful zoom toward the window at 13:07. Wispy tail, glow trail and stained-glass reflections with soft secondary motion.
LIGHTING: jewel-toned stained-glass colour pooling and reflecting on dark marble, warm-cool contrast, volumetric shafts of coloured light, the ghost's soft subsurface glow, then cool blue-white moonlight flooding in at the finale.
EFFECTS: glowing ghost light trail, drifting dust motes in light shafts, floor reflections, spiral-eye dizzy stars at 09:22, dimming glow and tiny tears at 11:15, bright moonlight burst and sparkle trail at 13:07.
ATMOSPHERE: enchanted-eerie yet whimsical and heartwarming, dreamy melancholic wonder building to hopeful triumphant relief, playful comedic timing.
AUDIO (if supported): soft magical music box and gentle orchestral strings, airy whooshes as the ghost darts and speeds up the stairs, a dizzy comedic wobble sting at 09:22, a soft sad sigh and fading twinkle at 11:15, a bright swelling uplifting chord with a happy chime and creaking window at 13:07.

NEGATIVE / AVOID: changing the ghost's design, colour or size, extra ghosts, extra characters or people, a real exit door instead of the window, scary or horror tone, flat lighting, watercolour or 2D flat cartoon style, distorted shapes, text or watermark, repeated identical camera angle in a row.

SHOT 1 — THE STANDOFF [0.0s – 1.9s]
Shot type & camera: Wide establishing shot, eye level, slow creeping push-in.
Scene direction: A dim neon-lit private dining room, red paper lanterns glowing, cigarette smoke drifting through the air. The silver-haired boss sits calmly at the head of the long black lacquer table; his suited men flank him. Across the table the tattooed rival and his crew stand tense in heavy silence. No one moves. Smoke curls, lanterns sway faintly.
Dialogue: None.
SFX: Low ominous room tone, faint distant city hum, a single ice cube settling in a glass, tense silence.
Camera direction: Slow creeping dolly-in down the length of the table toward the boss.

SHOT 2 — THE SAKE CUP [1.9s – 3.8s]
Shot type & camera: Medium shot, static hold with subtle life.
Scene direction: The boss lifts a small sake cup with a steady scarred hand, utterly unbothered. His sharp calm eyes never leave the rival across the table. Cigarette smoke curls around his composed face, red lantern light warming his features.
Dialogue: Boss (calm, quiet, menacing): "Sit. Drink. We are still civilised men."
SFX: Soft pour-settle of sake, faint smoke hiss, quiet tense ambience.
Camera direction: Static hold with a barely perceptible drift, smoke animated in foreground.

SHOT 3 — THE OUTBURST [3.8s – 5.6s]
Shot type & camera: Medium shot, static with a sharp micro-shake on impact.
Scene direction: The tattooed rival SLAMS both fists down on the black lacquer table. Dishes rattle and jump, sake cups spill, his dragon irezumi flexing across bared arms, teeth clenched, veins standing out in fury.
Dialogue: Rival (shouting, enraged): "Civilised?! You buried my brother!"
SFX: Violent table slam, dishes rattling and clattering, sake splashing, angry shout echoing.
Camera direction: Static hold with a hard camera-shake jolt on the slam.

SHOT 4 — COLD SMILE [5.6s – 7.5s]
Shot type & camera: Close-up, static with very slow push-in.
Scene direction: The boss's face fills the frame — completely unmoving, a cold half-smile curling his lips, the deep scar catching red lantern light, a lit cigarette between his fingers, a single trail of smoke crossing frame. Utterly unafraid.
Dialogue: Boss (soft, chilling): "And now... you'll join him."
SFX: Slow smoke exhale, faint crackle of cigarette, low tension drone rising.
Camera direction: Slow intimate push-in on the boss's cold eyes and half-smile.

SHOT 5 — HANDS MOVE [7.5s – 9.4s]
Shot type & camera: Dynamic low-angle shot, quick push-in.
Scene direction: The rival's men suddenly reach into their jackets; the boss's subordinates rise sharply in response. Chairs scrape, coats swing, hands hover near hidden weapons — the whole room coils to snap. Neon light streaks across tense faces.
Dialogue: None.
SFX: Scraping chairs, rustle of jackets, sharp collective intake of breath, rising tension sting.
Camera direction: Fast low-angle push-in as everyone rises, slight tilt for menace.

SHOT 6 — THE INSTANT BEFORE [9.4s – 11.3s]
Shot type & camera: Extreme close-up split staging, static locked hold.
Scene direction: A tattooed hand grips a katana hilt while a suited hand grips a pistol under the table — knuckles white, the frozen breath-held instant before violence erupts. Neon glints hard off steel.
Dialogue: None.
SFX: Metallic scrape of a blade half-drawn, click of a pistol hammer, dead silence, single heartbeat thump.
Camera direction: Locked-off macro hold, faint slow zoom, all sound dropping to near-silence.

SHOT 7 — CHAOS ERUPTS [11.3s – 13.1s]
Shot type & camera: Dynamic action shot, fast whip-pan with motion blur.
Scene direction: The rival LUNGES across the table with a flashing blade; dishes, sake and food explode upward in a shower of motion, the boss's men surging in. Full sakuga chaos — steel flashing, neon streaks, bodies colliding, smoke ripping apart. Peak violence.
Dialogue: Rival (roaring): "DIE!"
SFX: Explosive crash of shattering dishes, ringing steel clash, gunshot crack, shouting, chaotic impact.
Camera direction: Fast whip-pan following the lunge with heavy motion blur and quick shake.

SHOT 8 — SILENCE AFTER THE STORM [13.1s – 15.0s]
Shot type & camera: Wide finale shot, slow chilling pull-out.
Scene direction: Sudden dead stillness. The boss stands untouched over the fallen tattooed rival, calmly straightening his suit cuff. Smoke settles over the wrecked table and scattered, groaning men. Red lanterns swing gently overhead, casting slow-moving shadows.
Dialogue: Boss (quiet, final): "In this world... the last supper is always someone else's."
SFX: Settling debris, dripping sake, a swinging lantern creak, one final exhaled breath, cold silence.
Camera direction: Slow reverent pull-out revealing the wrecked room, smoke drifting into neon, soft bloom filling the frame.

Audio: Diegetic sound only — natural ambience, environmental foley, and subject-driven sound.
